iOS 27 launches this week with a brand-new Siri AI. David Pogue put the new Siri through 125 requests—here are the results.

iOS 27's new Siri AI impresses, earning high marks from David Pogue after 125 tests

Siri has been built into the iPhone for nearly 15 years. Yet for years, many Apple users have only come to rely on Siri for a limited set of supported tasks.

For example, I've always relied on Siri to set reminders, start timers, and play Apple Music—and to send messages while driving. But beyond those few limited functions, Siri's many shortcomings have kept me from relying on it too heavily.

But iOS 27's new Siri AI is a major upgrade, with capabilities that go far beyond what came before. Still, it may take some time to make it your go-to tool.

That's why I found David Pogue's latest Substack post so useful. Titled "125 Tests of the New AI Siri," it lists the more than 100 commands Pogue threw at Siri AI and details how it performed.

Here are a few examples that stood out to me:

28. What is everyone waiting on me to do? (It compiled a list from mail, messages, and reminders. Wild. Everything I'm doing for this column was supposed to be just for testing—but this one actually found some things I'd forgotten to do!) … 30. (Rushing late to a party:) What's the apartment number? ("Tonight's Bynum party is Unit 10-F." Note: I never mentioned which party or which day!) … 46. Delete all my alarms. ("Do you want to delete 38 alarms in 'Clock'?" Tap to confirm.)

Across these 125 tests, Siri succeeded at nearly all of them. The few failures—like sending a Venmo payment—should improve once third-party apps update to be compatible with iOS 27 and Siri AI.

You can check out all 125 of Pogue's Siri AI test examples over at his Substack.

How has your experience with Siri been on iOS 27? Let us know in the comments.
